authority: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science 9618 syllabus, 2027-2029, Version 2

records.resolution: Teaches selection and use of INTEGER, REAL, CHAR, STRING, BOOLEAN, DATE, ARRAY and FILE as the exact Cambridge pseudocode type set, including value-based selection boundaries.
Explains that a record groups named fields of different data types under one identifier and distinguishes field names from array indexes.
Directly teaches index, lower bound and upper bound and uses them consistently in declarations, traversal and boundary calculations.
Requires students to select one-dimensional or two-dimensional arrays from the logical shape of the data rather than from superficial scenario wording.
Adds complete Cambridge declarations, reads, writes and traversals for one-dimensional and two-dimensional arrays, including nested loops for two dimensions.
Provides full linear-search and ascending bubble-sort pseudocode, so traces no longer substitute for the required algorithms.
Explains persistence as the reason files are needed and teaches complete OPENFILE, READFILE/WRITEFILE, EOF and CLOSEFILE patterns for one or more text lines.
Uses the official definition of an abstract data type as a collection of data and a set of operations on those data, then applies it to stack, queue and linked list.
Compares LIFO stack, FIFO queue and linked-list traversal/editing features and requires a justified structure choice for a stated purpose.
Covers adding, editing and deleting data in array implementations of stacks, queues and linked lists, while preserving the syllabus boundary that ADT pseudocode is not required.
Quiz items now directly assess CHAR and DATE selection, dimensionality and declaration, and record field save/read operations without changing quiz totals.
Monthly and stage-review questions now require a complete bubble-sort algorithm and reasoned add/edit/delete behaviour across the three ADTs, with mark points aligned to the syllabus boundary.
Replaces incomplete or clipped visuals with deterministic 1536x1024 assets showing all eight pseudocode types and the define/save/read record relationship.
Adds deterministic visuals for the official ADT definition and array implementations of stack, queue and linked list, including the no-pseudocode-required boundary.
